title: Finite reduction of the completed algebra along an extended ideal
statement: Let R and S be commutative rings, I a finitely generated ideal of R, and φ : R → S a ring homomorphism. Put J = IS, Â = lim R/I^k and B̂ = lim S/J^k [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Assume S/J is a finitely generated R/I-module via the induced quotient homomorphism [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let ψ : Â → B̂ be a ring homomorphism such that for every k, x and r, if the kth coordinate of x is r modulo I^k then the kth coordinate of ψ(x) is φ(r) modulo J^k. Give B̂ the Â-module structure via ψ and put K = IÂ. Then B̂/KB̂ is a finitely generated Â/K-module via the quotient module action.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0394 (lemma-finite-after-completion), final paragraph; Lemma Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), parts (1) and (2). Source read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0394 and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05GG because the local literature copy is absent.

proof.text: Put A = AdicCompletion I R, J = map φ I, B = AdicCompletion J S, and K = map (R → A) I. Apply the coordinate condition to the canonical image of r in A, and use joint injectivity of evalₐ to prove ψ ∘ (R → A) = (S → B) ∘ φ. Ideal.map_map then gives map ψ K = map (S → B) J. This avoids comparing module completions.

Let e : B → S/J be evalOneₐ J and q : R/I → S/J the quotient homomorphism induced by φ. Choose a representative r for evalₐ I 1 x, use the coordinate condition at k = 1, and compose with the quotient factor maps to prove e ∘ ψ = q ∘ evalOneₐ I.

The ideal J is finitely generated by Ideal.FG.map applied to hI. Apply the completion quotient theorem to the ring S and ideal J: evalOneₐ J is surjective and its kernel is map (S → B) J. Ideal.smul_top_eq_map and the ideal equality above identify its kernel, as an A-submodule, with K • ⊤. Give S/J its A-algebra structure through e ∘ ψ; the evaluation e is A-linear by multiplicativity.

The given finiteness says q is a finite ring homomorphism. Since evalOneₐ I is surjective, it is a finite ring homomorphism by RingHom.Finite.of_surjective. RingHom.Finite.comp and the scalar compatibility above make S/J finite as an A-module. LinearMap.quotKerEquivOfSurjective for e identifies B/(K • ⊤) with S/J as A-modules, and Module.Finite.equiv transports finiteness. Finally Module.Finite.of_restrictScalars_finite enlarges scalars from A to A/K, with the canonical quotient scalar tower, giving the assertion.

proof_origin.place: Algebra, Tag 0394 final paragraph and Tag 05GG (2). Direct ring-completion quotient proof: compare extended ideals using coordinates, apply ker_evalOneₐ_eq_map to J, and transport finiteness via the evaluation quotient. Formalized by D3, 2026-10-13.

mathlib_searches.query: The quotient of completion of an algebra S along extended ideal I by the extended ideal in completion of R is finite over the residue quotient of completed R when S/IS is finite over R/I
For a finitely generated ideal I and ring homomorphism R to S, if S modulo IS is finite over R modulo I, then completion of S for IS is finite over completion of R for I

lean.statement: theorem extendedCompletion_module_reduction (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (I : Ideal R) (φ : R →+* S) (hI : I.FG) (hfinite : letI := (Ideal.quotientMap (Ideal.map φ I) φ Ideal.le_comap_map).toAlgebra Module.Finite (R ⧸ I) (S ⧸ Ideal.map φ I)) (ψ : AdicCompletion I R →+* AdicCompletion (Ideal.map φ I) S) (hψ : ∀ (k : ℕ) (x : AdicCompletion I R) (r : R), AdicCompletion.evalₐ I k x = Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ k) r → AdicCompletion.evalₐ (Ideal.map φ I) k (ψ x) = Ideal.Quotient.mk ((Ideal.map φ I) ^ k) (φ r)) : letI := ψ.toAlgebra let K := I.map (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion I R)) Module.Finite (AdicCompletion I R ⧸ K) (AdicCompletion (Ideal.map φ I) S ⧸ (K • ⊤ : Submodule (AdicCompletion I R) (AdicCompletion (Ideal.map φ I) S)))
